root_cause.text: In `net/tls/tls_do_encryption()`, the `-EBUSY` async-encryption error path performed cleanup twice—after `tls_encrypt_async_wait()` failed, it still ran the synchronous `encrypt_pending` decrement and scatterlist restoration even though `tls_encrypt_done()` had already done so, corrupting the `encrypt_pending` state and enabling a later use-after-free of `tls_rec`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch comment states that “the async callback tls_encrypt_done() has already decremented encrypt_pending and restored the sge on both success and error” and adds an early `list_del(&rec->list); return rc;` for `rc != -EINPROGRESS`, specifically to “skip the synchronous cleanup below on error”; the CVE description says the old code “double-decrement[s] encrypt_pending and double-restore[s] the scatterlist,” causing pending callbacks to run after the record is freed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid double cleanup after asynchronous TLS encryption completion by returning early on error and removing the record once.
intent_record.what: In tls_do_encryption(), after handling rc == -EBUSY by waiting for async completion, the code now checks whether the returned rc is not -EINPROGRESS. If so, it deletes the current record from the list and returns immediately, instead of falling through to the synchronous cleanup path. A comment was added explaining that tls_encrypt_done() already decrements encrypt_pending and restores the SGE on both success and error.
intent_record.how: This changes the error path for asynchronous encryption completion so that cleanup is not performed twice. On async failure, the record is removed and the function exits immediately, avoiding an extra decrement/cleanup that would otherwise corrupt state or double-handle the completed request.

grouping_result.intent: Avoid double cleanup after asynchronous TLS encryption completion by returning early on error and removing the record once.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes double cleanup in the async TLS encryption path by returning early on error and ensuring the record is removed only once, preventing the corrupted state that could lead to use-after-free.

candidates.rationale: This condition allowed the code to enter the cleanup path after an async-encryption completion/error case instead of returning early, causing the synchronous decrement and cleanup to run even when tls_encrypt_done() had already performed them.
This is the double-executed cleanup operation that corrupts encrypt_pending when the async path has already completed cleanup in tls_encrypt_done(), matching the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This branch allowed execution to fall into the post-encryption cleanup path even after an async encryption failure/completion case, instead of returning early. That led to cleanup being performed a second time after tls_encrypt_done() had already handled it.

This cleanup decremented encrypt_pending a second time in the async -EBUSY path after tls_encrypt_done() had already done so, corrupting the state and contributing to the later use-after-free of tls_rec.
